The current bug report is about how PosixParser ignores unrecognized tokens starting with '-' when stopAtNonOption is enabled; it silently skips them instead of treating them as errors (e.g., options that are not defined). The failing test case `testUnrecognizedOption2()` is designed to check this behavior: it expects an UnrecognizedOptionException to be thrown when an unknown option "-z" is encountered.

Because the method `PosixParser.parse(Options, String[])` is overloaded or ambiguous, it is unclear which exact method is used in the test, so I will focus on `PosixParser.flatten(Options, String[], boolean)`, which is typical in parsers to preprocess or handle argument tokens and options normalization. This method may be responsible for interpreting the tokens and might be ignoring unknown options starting with '-' incorrectly.

I will now inspect the method `PosixParser.flatten(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[], boolean)` since the boolean parameter likely corresponds to stopAtNonOption, which relates to this bug. This method is the most likely place where unrecognized token handling is controlled.
